name: Epic Charging
tagline: Cloud-Native EV Fleet Depot Management & Take-Home Reimbursement Platform
overview: Epic Charging is a modern, cloud-native EV charging management software platform built specifically for commercial fleets, municipal operations, and multi-tenant depots. Founded in 2021 by electric mobility veterans from ChargePoint and Nissan, Epic Charging provides an intuitive single-pane-of-glass dashboard for monitoring charger uptime, executing automated load balancing, managing take-home employee vehicle charging reimbursement, and processing multi-fleet billing.

key_features.title: Smart Depot Load Management
key_features.description: Dynamically throttles and schedules energy delivery across active chargers to ensure commercial vehicles are ready for dispatch without exceeding site utility power limits.

key_features.title: Take-Home Fleet Reimbursement
key_features.description: Automates tracking, utility rate calculation, and expense reimbursement for commercial drivers charging take-home fleet vehicles at their personal residences.

key_features.title: Remote Diagnostics & Auto-Healing
key_features.description: Continuously monitors OCPP heartbeats, automatically detects fault codes, triggers soft resets, and alerts technicians before vehicle routes are impacted.

key_features.title: Multi-Tenant Fleet Billing
key_features.description: Allows shared commercial depots to separate billing, assign custom electricity tariffs, and generate automated invoices for different fleet departments or subcontracted carriers.

key_features.title: Access Control & Driver Authentication
key_features.description: Supports seamless vehicle authorization via RFID cards, mobile apps, QR codes, and automated vehicle identification (Autocharge / ISO 15118).

hardware_compatibility: 100% hardware-agnostic. Pre-integrated and certified with over 50+ OCPP charger models including ABB, Autel, BTC Power, ChargePoint, Delta, Enel X, Grizzl-E, Siemens, and Wallbox.
pricing_model: Predictable monthly or annual SaaS subscription per connected charging port, with tiered enterprise depot pricing.
pros: Modern, intuitive UI engineered by electric mobility veterans
Built-in employee home charging reimbursement tracking for take-home fleet programs
Extensive hardware library supporting 50+ certified OCPP charger models
Automated fault detection and remote charger healing reduces on-site maintenance visits
Fast depot deployment with pre-configured charger onboarding templates
considerations: Younger startup compared to multi-decade telematics providers
Primary market focus is currently North America and select international deployments

faqs.question: What is Epic Charging and who is it designed for?
faqs.answer: Epic Charging is a cloud-based EV fleet charging and energy management software platform designed for commercial fleets, municipalities, and multi-tenant depot operators who need an intuitive, hardware-agnostic solution for depot charging, load management, and driver reimbursement.

faqs.question: How does Epic Charging solve take-home fleet charging reimbursement?
faqs.answer: Epic Charging connects to compatible home chargers used by fleet drivers, tracks kilowatt-hours consumed exclusively by company vehicles, matches usage against local utility electricity rates, and automatically generates audit-ready reimbursement reports.

faqs.question: Does Epic Charging work with any EV charger brand?
faqs.answer: Yes. Epic Charging is built entirely on open standards (OCPP 1.6J and 2.0.1) and is pre-tested with over 50 charger hardware manufacturers, preventing costly hardware vendor lock-in.

faqs.question: Can multiple fleets share a single charging facility with Epic Charging?
faqs.answer: Yes. Epic Charging includes multi-tenant fleet billing, enabling multiple companies, departments, or contractors to share depot charging stations while receiving separate, automated electricity usage invoices.

faqs.question: How does Epic Charging integrate with telematics platforms like Geotab and Samsara?
faqs.answer: Epic Charging integrates via secure APIs to ingest vehicle odometer readings, battery State of Charge (SoC), and dispatch schedules, ensuring charging is timed to meet route demands.
